what: Encode of the decoded twitter.cbor through ref_binding with sharedrefs::off, microseconds per document. Arm old: main c5efb0b. Arm new: when the walk ends with nesting_depth_exceeded and the binding answers value_identity, a cold search walks the value again with the identities of the ancestors (as encoding/json of Go and json of Python keep their markers) and throws cbor::cyclic_data_structure, a std::logic_error, when a child is its own ancestor.
why: The owner decided that encode without sharedrefs::on throws a usage error on a cycle. A first prototype kept the unwinding values in every node and cost 10 percent (295 against 266 us); this one does nothing on the path that succeeds.
how: Google Benchmark, one binary per arm, each built twice (a, b). 3 rounds alternating, --benchmark_min_time=0.1s --benchmark_repetitions=3, random interleaving, GLIBC_TUNABLES trim_threshold, mmap_threshold and top_pad high. Behaviour checked once: 28([29(0)]) throws with off and encodes with on; 70 nested arrays give nesting_depth_exceeded as a value.

context.commit: mbedded-cbor main c5efb0b, arm new is a patch on it
